dedupe_keys.name: fly tipping statistics for england defra wastedataflow local authority returns

description: This official statistics series counts fly-tipping incidents, that is illegal dumping of waste, reported by local authorities in England and the enforcement actions they took. It is published by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs from the returns councils make to the WasteDataFlow system. The release covers every local authority in England by financial year from 2007-08 onwards and gives incidents by waste type (household, construction and demolition, green, white goods, tyres, clinical and others), by land type (highways, footpaths, back alleys, council land, private land), by size (from a single bin bag to tipper lorry loads), estimated clearance costs, and actions such as warning letters, fixed penalty notices and prosecutions. Tables are free to download in CSV and spreadsheet form with a methods note, under the Open Government Licence v3.0, and the release is updated annually, most recently on 25 February 2026. Caveats: figures depend on how actively each council records incidents, most private-land dumping and large incidents handled by the Environment Agency are excluded, and cost figures are estimates. Simulation uses: mapping demand for waste enforcement and clearance services, modelling informal waste flows in collection service disruptions, and using post-flood or strike spikes to test resilience of waste collection. Related records: the ENV18 local authority collected waste statistics (data-defra-env18-local-authority-collected-waste) come from the same WasteDataFlow system.
